harness.name: watermark-off-full-prewarm-workers1-warm
limits: Collector delivery adds latency to observation; app elapsed and host monotonic origins differ.
One fresh process; SQLite may already be running.
The new kernel disables only successful-allocation watermark diagnostics relative to the retained instrumented-off baseline; failure diagnostics and allocator algorithms are unchanged.
Both detailed guest allocation tracing and allocation/free ABI breadcrumbs are already disabled in both kernels.
Both kernels use the same old eacb application with one explicit async worker and original provider-gated initial prewarm. This is not a worker-count or new-prewarm-policy experiment.
The new no-input window is thirty host seconds after observing attachment; baseline controls used five. Readiness booleans and draft-echo latency are therefore not equivalent-condition comparisons.
One cold-service process and one warm-service process per setting do not establish repeatable performance effects; caches, service state, remote responses and stored session data can vary.
Host mono_ms and application elapsed_ms have different origins. Correlate by request within the boot; no combined end-to-end total is inferred.
Nested phases overlap; elapsed polls and scheduler continuations are wall time, not CPU consumption.
First-flush/readiness markers measure source events, not physical terminal presentation or every submission guard.
Only recognized timing fields and controlled-test metadata are retained.
